brief: A 10-second cinematic film of the Golden Gate Bridge at sunrise: open on fog rolling across the bay with the bridge small in the distance, then a shot gliding beneath the bridge deck, and end looking out to the open ocean with the title 'Golden Hour'.
checks: Does the opening shot show visible fog moving across the bay?
Is the fog’s motion smooth and continuous (no jerky or constant‑speed movement)?
Is the Golden Gate Bridge visible but small in the frame during the opening shot (occupying less than about one‑fifth of the frame height)?
Does the transition from the fog shot to the beneath‑deck shot occur without a hard cut or abrupt jump (the camera movement continues fluidly)?
In the beneath‑deck shot, does the camera glide smoothly under the bridge deck with the deck visible above and water below (no static frame)?
Does the motion beneath the deck ease in at its start and ease out before the next transition (no constant‑speed linear movement)?
Does the final shot reveal a clear view of the open‑ocean horizon, with the bridge no longer dominating the frame?
Does the text ‘Golden Hour’ appear in the final shot, centered horizontally and vertically within the title‑safe area, legible and at least about one‑tenth of the frame height in size?
Does the text fade in with an ease‑in, hold steady for at least half a second, and then fade out (or remain) without an abrupt appearance/disappearance?
Is there no period longer than half a second where the picture is static with no meaningful change (i.e., something moves or changes each second)?
Does the video begin with visual content immediately (no black screen or empty frames) for the first half‑second?
Does the final frame hold still for at least half a second before the video ends (the last half‑second is a frozen frame of ocean + title)?
Are there no observable glitches, flicker, overlapping text, or rendering artifacts throughout the video?
Does the picture fill the entire frame with no black bars, borders, masks, or hard‑edged vignettes?
